title: Palms Up Together Emoji 🤲 Meaning: Dua and Open Hands
description: 🤲 shows two cupped, upturned palms. It is widely used for dua, the Muslim prayer of supplication, and for offering, receiving or asking. Here is how it is read.
summary: The 🤲 palms up together emoji shows two open hands held side by side with palms facing up. Its best-known meaning is prayer, especially dua, the personal supplication made by Muslims. It also represents offering or receiving something, asking humbly, and the sign for “book” in American Sign Language.
meaning: For many Muslims this is the prayer emoji. During dua, a person raises both hands with palms open toward the sky and asks God for help, forgiveness or blessings. 🤲 matches that posture exactly, so it accompanies “ameen,” “make dua for me,” Ramadan and Eid greetings, and condolences. Where a Christian user might send 🙏, a Muslim user will often choose this one.

Outside religion, cupped hands suggest giving and receiving. People use it when presenting something (“here you go 🤲”), holding something precious, or asking for a handout. A popular meme style places a small object above the hands, such as 🤲💖 or 🤲🥺, as though gently offering up or cradling it. The tone is tender, meaning “this is for you” or “I will protect this.”

Pleading is a related sense. The gesture resembles a beggar's open hands, so it turns up in joking requests: “spare notes from today's lecture? 🤲.” It conveys humility and need more strongly than folded hands, because the palms are literally waiting to be filled. Used sincerely, the same image suits appeals for donations and messages of thanks for help received.

In American Sign Language, placing the palms together and opening them like a cover is the sign for “book,” and the emoji is sometimes used with that meaning by signers and in reading-related posts. That use is uncommon compared with prayer and offering, but it explains why some keyboards return this emoji for the search word “book.”

contexts.label: In Muslim communities
contexts.body: It appears every day in messages asking for or promising prayers, and in large numbers during Ramadan, on Fridays, at Eid and during Hajj. After news of a death, illness or hardship, 🤲 means “may God make it easy” or “praying for you.” Common partners are the crescent moon, the Kaaba and the mosque emoji.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Secular use centers on asking and offering. It softens a request with a touch of humor, presents a gift or a piece of news with care, and expresses gratitude for something received. Next to a pleading face it is an exaggerated beg. Beside a heart it says the sender is handing over their affection.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: Fans use it to hold up things they adore, such as a favorite character, a tiny animal or a new song, as if cupping them in their hands. Charity and fundraising posts use it for giving and receiving aid. In wellness content it stands for openness, receiving blessings and gratitude without tying the message to any particular faith.

examples.text: Please keep my grandmother in your duas 🤲
examples.meaning: A request for prayers in the Islamic tradition.
Affirming a prayer someone else has shared.

examples.text: Ramadan Mubarak to you and your family 🤲🌙
examples.meaning: A greeting for the holy month, with a prayerful tone.
Presenting a gift, as if holding it out with both hands.

examples.text: Look at this kitten 🤲 must protect
examples.meaning: Cradling something precious, in a figurative sense.

combos.meaning: Prayer during Ramadan or another Islamic occasion.
Offering love or holding something dear.
Supplication connected to Mecca, Hajj or Umrah.

confusedWith.difference: 🙏 presses the palms together, read as Christian prayer, namaste, please or thank you. 🤲 opens the palms upward, the posture of Islamic dua and of receiving. Both can mean “praying for you,” but they reflect different traditions.
👐 shows two open palms facing forward, as in a hug, jazz hands or openness. 🤲 turns the palms up and cups them together to hold or receive something. Orientation separates embracing from asking.
🫴 is a single hand with the palm up, used for offering, beckoning or presenting. 🤲 uses both hands together and carries the stronger association with prayer and humble requests.

avoid: Do not use it mockingly in reference to Muslim prayer.
Avoid the joking beggar use in conversations about real poverty or need.
Do not substitute it for 🙏 when you simply mean “thank you” to someone unfamiliar with it; they may be unsure what you mean.
design: Two open hands side by side, little fingers touching, palms turned upward as if holding water or an open book. Platforms differ slightly in how cupped the hands appear and the viewing angle, but the pose is the same everywhere. It was added in 2017 and supports skin tones.

faqs.a: It represents dua, the act of personally asking God for something. Muslims commonly raise their open palms while making dua, so the emoji is used with prayers, “ameen,” and religious greetings throughout the year.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🤲 and 🙏?
faqs.a: The hands are open and upturned in 🤲 and pressed together in 🙏. Both can mean prayer. Folded hands also mean please and thank you, while palms up together also means offering, receiving or begging.

faqs.q: What does 🤲 mean from a guy or a girl?
faqs.a: Either a prayerful message, such as “praying for you,” or a gentle offering or request. With hearts or cute emojis, they are presenting affection or pleading playfully. It is not a flirtation signal by itself.

In American Sign Language, opening the palms like a book is the sign for “book,” and the emoji can be used that way. Most people will not read it so, however; for reading, the 📚 or 📖 emoji is clearer.

Yes. Nothing restricts it to one faith, and it has general meanings of offering, receiving and asking. It is respectful to be aware of its strong association with Islamic prayer and to avoid using it flippantly in that context.
